scenes.text: Learn a new word, and suddenly you see it everywhere.
It's called the frequency illusion, or the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon.
The odd name comes from a reader's letter to a Minnesota newspaper in nineteen ninety-four.
The reader had just heard of a German group called Baader-Meinhof, then kept spotting the name.
Linguist Arnold Zwicky gave it the name frequency illusion in two thousand five.
Your brain starts filtering for the new thing, so you notice what was always there.
What have you suddenly started seeing everywhere?

title: Why new things suddenly appear everywhere 👀
caption: The frequency illusion: once you notice something new, your brain's selective attention makes it seem to pop up everywhere. Linguist Arnold Zwicky named it in 2005. 👀
